findings.where: Hero, the two-line Cinzel heading 'MARK · M · MOSELEY / INFRASTRUCTURE · ADVISOR' (desktop; on phone the role runs to two lines under the name)
findings.fault: The name and the role are the same size, weight and red. The role line is much longer, so at a squint it outweighs the name: on desktop it runs about 960 px against the name's 670 px and is wider than the mark above it. The eye lands on 'Infrastructure Advisor', a job title, before it lands on the man.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose brief says the individual is the brand. A bank officer scanning the first screen takes away a category ('infrastructure advisor') before a person's name, which is the firm voice the brand sheet rejects.

findings.where: Two-column bands on desktop: Palette beside Texture, and An Article Page beside Motion Sketch
findings.fault: Each pair is laid out at the height of its taller half, so the shorter half leaves an empty hole: about 180 px of bare ground under the palette notes, and about 280 px under the article's link row while the motion-sketch box runs on. The page ends ragged on the left, and the rhythm between sections is set by whichever column happens to be longer.
findings.who_objects: The layout round's designer, who inherits a grid with no even section spacing, and any visitor who reads the hole under the article as the page having ended.

findings.where: Article specimen, the pull-quote tablet beside the hero's 'WRITE TO MARK' tablet (worst on phone, where the quote's dark dovetails are the heaviest shapes in the article)
findings.fault: By similarity, the pull quote has the same dovetail-handled tablet shape as the one button, but the quote cannot be clicked. In the article, the only shape that looks like the call to action does nothing, and it sits where a reader expects a button.
findings.who_objects: A reader on an article page who taps the boxed quote expecting it to act. Angélique too: every post she adds with a quote puts a second button-shaped tablet on the page.

findings.where: Motion sketch, the timeline table's column heads 'START LENGTH EASING' (desktop)
findings.fault: The first column takes most of the width, so the three heads and their values sit packed together on the right. By proximity, 'START LENGTH EASING' reads as one phrase rather than three columns, and the figures beneath crowd each other.
findings.who_objects: The animator on #9, who reads this table for start times and lengths and has to check which figure belongs to which column.

findings.where: Article specimen, the post title 'THE WORLD'S BEST PUBLIC-PRIVATE PARTNERSHIP LAW' (desktop)
findings.fault: The title is held to about half the article column and breaks into three short lines. Its block is much narrower than the body text under it, so the heading and the body don't share a left-and-right edge.
findings.who_objects: Angélique adding posts with longer titles, which will stack into four or five lines of capitals, and a reader whose first view of an article is a tall narrow block of red.
